DOM elements in a Qt Widgets window

Qt Quick renders with WebGL, and an earlier page gave it DOM elements as textures. Qt Widgets, the older and more widely used Qt toolkit, paints every window in software and copies the changed pixels to a 2D canvas with putImageData(). This page loads a Qt Widgets 6.10 app and draws real elements into the window's canvas with drawElementImage() after each of those copies. Load the app, then tap a field to type, scroll the window, move the slider, or open the Qt combo box above the fields.

ResultExperimentDetail

Findings

  • Yes, with one wrapped method. Qt for WebAssembly paints a Qt Widgets window with its raster engine and copies the changed rectangles to a 2D canvas with putImageData(). The page wraps putImageData() on that canvas's context and calls drawElementImage() for each element straight after it. Qt 6.10.3 is unchanged. Measured in Chromium 157.
  • No geometry call is needed. In a 2D canvas drawElementImage() also sets the hit box, so a tap lands on the field where Qt laid out its widget. An element whose widget is scrolled out isn't drawn and is made inert.
  • The canvas is Qt's, inside a shadow root. Qt creates canvas.qt-window-canvas in the shadow root of a child of the container. The page adds the layoutsubtree and content="drawable" attributes after Qt made it and appends the elements to it. Styles from the page don't reach the shadow root, so the page copies each element's computed style inline first.
  • Layout goes both ways through heightForWidth(). Qt's layout gives the widget a width in resizeEvent(), the element takes that width, and the widget answers heightForWidth() with the element's offsetHeight.
  • A Qt popup covers the fields with no guard code. The QComboBox list is a second Qt window, which is a second canvas above the first one, so the browser's own hit testing gives the popup the tap.
  • Drawing after the flush doesn't loop. drawElementImage() outside a paint event doesn't cause a paint event. A change in an element fires paint, the widget calls update(), Qt flushes and the elements are drawn again: one paint event, two flushes.
  • Qt overwrites the element on every flush of its rectangle. The widget fills its background in paintEvent(), so the element has to be drawn again after every flush. The page draws all of them after each one.
  • Touch scrolling is Qt's, and stops at an element. QScroller::grabGesture() on the viewport makes a touch drag scroll the area. A drag that starts on a DOM element doesn't scroll it, because the element stops the event before Qt's listeners.
  • Cost: 14 MB. The WebAssembly file is 14.1 MB before compression, so the app loads after a tap on this page.

Source: native/qt-widgets-dom. The binary is statically linked against the open-source edition of Qt 6.10.3 (LGPL-3.0 and GPL-3.0). Its complete source is that folder plus Qt from download.qt.io.
